subject: Forced variant request for CloudHealth — tradeoffs and approval
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Rodriguez <anna@cloudhealth.io>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Forced variant request for CloudHealth — tradeoffs and approval

Team —

Quick background: CloudHealth is asking us to serve a single pinned model variant for their production traffic (no fallback, no cross-region routing) citing regulatory QA & deterministic output requirements for their billing reconciliation flows. They want the pin to a 8-bit quantized variant of Raven-34B (v3) in us-west to meet latency/throughput targets and to satisfy their internal audit.

Why this is escalated: their contract renewal is contingent on this guarantee. They explicitly requested a written product-side justification for disabling fallback and region failover. Legal also wants an ops runbook for how we’d handle capacity or the variant failing.

Ask: I need Ops + Product tradeoff bullets and a short recommendation (approve/deny/conditional) by EOD so I can respond to CloudHealth and share a mitigations runbook. Specifics that would be helpful:
- Expected p95 latency change vs standard routing (numbers)
- Failure-mode behavior if pinned variant hits OOM or degraded perf
- Cost delta (tokens and infra) vs standard smart-routing + fallback
- Security/compliance gaps if we limit cross-region failover

Attachments: I’m including the customer note and our early SLA impact spreadsheet.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Lead, Enterprise GTM
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: cloudhealth_forced_variant_rationale.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: sla-impact-estimates.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Rodriguez <anna@cloudhealth.io>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Forced variant request for CloudHealth — tradeoffs and approval

Jordan — thanks for the context. I spoke to Anna on the call this morning: the renewal T&Cs are pretty explicit that the model must be deterministic for monthly billing reconciliation and audits. They are willing to accept a short maintenance window SLA if we can provide a documented fallback process, but they prefer minimal automatic routing to other variants.

From a GTM perspective, this is high impact (> $1.2M ARR) and we should try to avoid a hard denial unless Ops/Product push back strongly. But we also have to be honest about the operational cost and support burden.

Irene — can you confirm whether a no-fallback regional lock is something we can offer as an enterprise exception, and what guardrails you'd require from Legal/CS?

Marissa
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Rodriguez <anna@cloudhealth.io>, CloudHealth Legal <legal@cloudhealth.io>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Forced variant request for CloudHealth — tradeoffs and approval

Jordan/Marissa —

Short answer: we can support a forced-variant + regional lock as an enterprise exception, but it needs the following guardrails and operational commitments from both sides:

1) Runbook + Pre-warm: Ops requires a pre-warm and capacity reservation for the pinned variant during business hours (we’d maintain a reserved pool in us-west). This reduces autoscaling flexibility and increases monthly committed costs.
2) Maintenance window & failover playbook: CloudHealth must accept a 30-minute scheduled maintenance window monthly for kernel/driver rollups and agree to a documented manual failover procedure (no automatic cross-variant fallback).
3) SLA & credits: Product and Legal must sign off on an adjusted SLA that includes a lower (longer) MTTR for forced-variant incidents where automatic fallback is disabled. Ops needs explicit buy-in for the adjusted credit exposure.
4) Observability hooks: We’ll expose per-variant tracing and a synthetic prompt-set health monitor (ops + customer) for early detection; Product will own regression thresholds.

Preliminary numbers: based on a quick run with the serving runtime team — p95 latency expected to be ~12% higher under peak load vs our smart-routing (because of reduced regional spillover), and we estimate a 22% infra cost uplift to hold reserved capacity (see attached SLA sheet).

Recommendation: Conditional approve subject to Legal signing the exception addendum (SLA adjustment + maintenance window) and Ops receiving commitment for a monthly reserved budget line. Product to own regression alerts and a canary prompt-set.

I’ll add a short ops-runbook draft and circulate for review.

—Irene
Director, Production Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Forced variant request for CloudHealth — tradeoffs and approval

Thanks for the quick answers, all. Adding a couple of product considerations & a suggested approach: 

Product notes:
- Determinism: If CloudHealth needs deterministic outputs for reconciliation, we should require a fixed model+tokenization snapshot (single pinned commit id) and a curated prompt set for QA. Product can provide a signed snapshot manifest that their auditors can reference.
- Observability: We’ll add a mandatory synthetic suite (30 prompts) that runs hourly to detect drift; failure triggers a paging policy to both Ops and the customer.
- Rollback plan: Because automatic fallback is disabled, Product recommends a staged pre-approved emergency fallback (manual) that can be invoked by SREs with a documented rollback checklist. This meets the customer's desire for determinism while giving us an escape hatch.

Suggested decision: Approve as a conditional enterprise exception. Conditions: legal exception addendum (Irene), a reserved capacity commit (Ops), signed snapshot manifest & synthetic prompt monitoring (Product). We should also price the change as a premium addon (25% uplift on their committed capacity) to cover the reservation and support burden.

If everyone agrees I’ll draft the product bullet points for the addendum and early-runbook language.

-Hannah Schmitt
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
